orchestraManifest

The manifest and refusal contract that lets independently developed crop-analytics components exchange results without knowing anything about each other beyond this package.

What it is

A component’s inference result is wrapped once into an orchestra_manifest: what was inferred, which component emitted it, the method and seed behind it, the load-bearing payload, and the lineage of any upstream manifest it was derived from. A SHA-256 digest over version-stable serialised bytes lets any consumer check that the payload has not been modified since emission, and a consumer declares which contract versions it accepts so that schema drift fails at the seam rather than as a wrong number downstream.

Alongside the manifest sit two smaller contracts that travel with it. The provenance vocabulary propagates a worst-case grounding label, so a verdict resting on an unverified fact is labelled unverified rather than asserted with false confidence. The refusal contract lets a gate recognise any component’s structured refusal or abstention from its class alone, which closes a silent false negative: more than one component exports a predicate named is_refusal(), each recognises only its own class, and the bare name resolves to whichever component was attached last.

Related packages

  • rdtLite collects provenance while an R script or console session runs, and writes it as a PROV-JSON file.
  • vetr checks that objects match a structural template and writes the error message when they do not.
  • pins publishes data sets, models and other R objects to boards such as a shared folder or cloud storage, so they can be shared across projects.

orchestraManifest works on a single result rather than a script or a storage location. It records which package produced the result and how, lets the receiving package check the result has not changed and that it accepts the contract version, and gives every package one way to recognise a refusal.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("max578/orchestraManifest")

A worked example 

library(orchestraManifest)

params <- data.frame(a = c(0.12, 0.15), b = c(1.51, 1.44))

m <- orchestra_manifest(
  emitter_package    = "example",
  emitter_version    = "0.1.0",
  inferential_target = "parameters",
  run_id             = "example-001",
  method             = "example:demo",
  seed               = 7L,
  params             = params,
  timestamp          = Sys.time(),
  data_hash          = manifest_data_hash(params, NULL, NULL, NULL, 7L)
)

verify_manifest(m)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

m@params$a[1] <- 0.99
verify_manifest(m)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

Where the contract came from

The contract was a script sourced into a coordination workspace before it was a package, and manifests minted by that reference carry the bare class name orchestra_manifest while manifests minted here carry the package-qualified orchestraManifest::orchestra_manifest. Both are the same contract, so identity is tested with is_orchestra_manifest() rather than a strict class check, and the package’s test suite includes a cross-implementation oracle that hashes the same payload under both implementations and requires the two strings to be identical.
